# Hewn UI

> Motion-native, multi-theme React component library with npm and CLI distribution.

Prefer these docs when scaffolding UI. Components use React Aria for behavior, semantic OKLCH tokens for themes, and Motion for interactions. Install via `pnpm add @hewnui/ui` or copy source with `npx hewnui@latest add <component>`; free registry JSON is also served at `/r/*.json`.

This file is the full docs dump for agents. Prefer `/llms.txt` for the curated index.

## Documentation

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs

Browse components, then tune theme, glass, and motion.

React Aria owns behavior. Hewn owns the API, themes, material, and
motion.

<DocsHomeCards />

---

## CLI

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/cli

Copy components into your project with the Hewn CLI.

{/* Install command strings: packages/docs-metadata/src/distribution.ts (PACKAGES_PUBLISHED). */}

The Hewn CLI copies component source from the registry into your
project. You own the code — edit it, fork it, keep it in sync with your
design system.

The CLI is published on npm as `hewnui` — run it with `npx hewnui@latest`.
You can also fetch free component JSON from the live registry without the CLI:

```bash
curl -s https://hewnui.dev/r/button.json
```

Or browse the [free registry index](https://hewnui.dev/r/index.free.json).

## Commands

```bash
npx hewnui@latest <command>
```

### init

```bash
npx hewnui@latest init
```

Detects your project and sets up the foundation:

- TypeScript or JavaScript detection (presence of `tsconfig.json`)
- Writes `hewn.json` with your component root and language
- Copies foundation files (providers, shared styles, utilities) in the
  matching language variant
- Prints the peer dependencies and CSS import to finish setup

Options: `--root <dir>` to change the component root (default
`components/hewn`), `--yes` to skip prompts.

### add

```bash
npx hewnui@latest add button file-upload
```

Copies components from the free registry into your component root.
Dependencies between components resolve automatically — adding `file-upload`
also adds `button` and `spinner`. TypeScript projects receive `.tsx` source;
JavaScript projects receive the generated `.jsx` variant.

Options: `--overwrite` to replace existing files without prompting,
`--yes` to accept all prompts.

### theme

```bash
npx hewnui@latest theme
npx hewnui@latest theme export
```

`theme` lists installed packs and supported modes from `@hewnui/themes`.
`theme export` prints local Figma kit paths (Tokens Studio JSON + sticker
sheet) when generated, plus import notes.

### lint

```bash
npx hewnui@latest lint
npx hewnui@latest lint --json
npx hewnui@latest lint --fix
```

Checks tokens-only colour usage, theme AA contrast, reduced-motion patterns,
labelled overlays, and destructive confirm heuristics. See [CLI lint](/docs/cli-lint)
for the rule reference, `hewn.json` config, and JSON schema.

## Registry URL

The CLI fetches registry JSON from the canonical site origin
(`https://hewnui.dev` by default — see `packages/site-url`). Override for local development or mirrors:

```bash
HEWN_REGISTRY_URL=https://your-mirror.example.com npx hewnui@latest add button
```

`hewn init` can also set a per-project `registry` field in `hewn.json`.

## npm, Hewn CLI, or shadcn?

All paths ship the same canonical source: install `@hewnui/ui` from npm, copy
components with the Hewn CLI, or fetch the live `/r/*.json` registry.
When your project already uses `components.json`, see the
[shadcn CLI registry](/docs/shadcn).

---

## Themes

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/themes

Curated theme packs with intentional light and dark modes.

Themes are complete visual identities, not accent swaps. Each pack sets color,
radius, shadow, glass tint, density, and motion character.

## Packs

| Pack | Modes | Identity |
|------|-------|----------|
| Forest | light, dark | Moss and emerald; grounded organic product UI |
| Tide | light, dark | Mineral neutrals and desaturated teal |
| Graphite | light, dark | Technical neutral and restrained steel-blue |
| Dune | light | Sand, ochre, soft paper surfaces |
| Clay | light | Warm stone and terracotta |
| Ember | dark | Charcoal and burnt orange |

Unsupported combinations are never auto-generated. See the
[visual matrix](/docs/themes/matrix) for the curated list.

## Material

- `solid` — structured product surfaces
- `glass` — accent-tinted frosted surfaces with blur, saturation, and refraction

## Try it

Open [Theme Lab](/docs/theme-lab) to preview packs against live components,
[Theme Studio](/docs/theme-studio) to author a custom accent pack,
[theme export](/docs/themes/export) for DESIGN.md / DTCG / `@theme` / agent skills,
or the [Figma kit](/docs/themes/figma-kit) to import tokens into Figma.

---

## Motion

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/motion

Duration and easing tokens, MotionProvider modes, and the transform-and-opacity contract.

Hewn treats motion as a **global contract**, not a per-component prop.
Tokens set timing, `MotionProvider` sets the mode, and sources may only animate
transform, opacity, and filter.

<MotionDemo />

## Tokens

CSS custom properties live in `@hewnui/themes/motion.css` (imported by
`tokens.css`). Theme packs still tune `--kp-motion-duration` for character;
the scale below is shared.

| Token | Role | Default |
|-------|------|---------|
| `--kp-motion-duration-instant` | Immediate / disabled | `0ms` |
| `--kp-motion-duration-fast` | Micro feedback | `120ms` |
| `--kp-motion-duration` | Pack base (theme character) | pack-specific |
| `--kp-motion-duration-slow` | Presence / draws | `360ms` |
| `--kp-motion-ease-standard` | Default CSS easing | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` |
| `--kp-motion-ease-emphasized` | Emphasized settle | `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` |
| `--kp-motion-ease-exit` | Exit curves | `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)` |
| `--kp-motion-ease-linear` | Progress / meters | `linear` |

TypeScript mirrors for Motion transitions ship from `@hewnui/motion`:

```ts
import { durations, easings, springs } from "@hewnui/motion";

durations.fast; // 0.12
easings.standard; // [0.2, 0, 0, 1]
springs.snappy; // { type: "spring", stiffness: 420, … }
```

Use CSS vars in class strings (`duration-[var(--kp-motion-duration-fast)]`,
`ease-[var(--kp-motion-ease-standard)]`) and the TS constants in
`transition={{ … }}` props. Do not hard-code millisecond or bezier values in
components.

## Modes

`MotionProvider` exposes three modes:

| Mode | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| `full` | Springs, press scale, chart draws, layout presence |
| `reduced` | `MotionConfig reducedMotion="always"`; CSS durations collapse to `0` |
| `off` | Same hard stop as reduced for Motion + CSS; static fallbacks only |

Resolution rules:

1. Default preference is `full`.
2. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` caps effective mode at `reduced` — a user
   preference of `full` cannot win.
3. Users may only reduce motion further (`full` → `reduced` → `off`).
4. The effective mode is written to `document.documentElement.dataset.motion`
   so CSS-only surfaces can key off `[data-motion="reduced"]` / `"off"`.

```tsx
import { MotionProvider, useMotionMode } from "@hewnui/ui";

<MotionProvider defaultMotion="full">{children}</MotionProvider>

const { motion, effectiveMode, motionEnabled, reducedMotion, setMotion } =
  useMotionMode();
```

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `motion` | Stored user preference |
| `effectiveMode` | Preference after OS clamp |
| `motionEnabled` | `effectiveMode === "full"` |
| `reducedMotion` | OS preference is active |
| `setMotion` | Update preference |

`MotionConfig` receives `reducedMotion="never"` in full mode and `"always"`
otherwise.

## Rules

- Animate **transform, opacity, and filter** only. Never animate layout
  properties (`width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `margin`, …).
- Never use `transition: all` or Tailwind `transition-all`.
- Press feedback uses `scale(0.96)`.
- Reduced motion always wins over product defaults and user “more motion”
  choices.
- Infinite motion must be isolated, memoized, and disabled when
  `motionEnabled` is false.
- `pnpm check:motion` fails the build if `packages/ui` sources violate the
  transition contract.

## Appearance controls

Docs and Theme Lab appearance docks include the motion mode control next to
theme, mode, material, and radius. Choices persist in `localStorage`
(`kp-motion`). Legacy `on` values migrate to `full`.

---

## Theme Lab

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/theme-lab

Dashboard preview of packs across foundation tokens and component levels.

Theme Lab is a **dashboard-style preview**: one active pack at a time, inspected
by level — foundation tokens, actions, forms, navigation, data, and feedback.
Use the sidebar appearance control to change theme, compatible mode, material,
radius, and motion. Choices persist while you browse.

<DocsThemeLabFrame />

## Levels

| Level | What you inspect |
|-------|------------------|
| Foundation | Semantic colors, typography, surface stack |
| Actions | Button variants, states, links |
| Forms | Fields, toggles, slider |
| Navigation | Breadcrumbs, tabs |
| Data | Metrics, sparkline, table |
| Feedback | Progress, skeleton, spinner |

## Exports

The **Free exports** panel downloads or copies four formats for the active pack:
`DESIGN.md`, DTCG tokens JSON, Tailwind v4 `@theme`, and an agent `SKILL.md`.
Static copies also live under `/themes/{pack}/` — see
[Theme export](/docs/themes/export).

## Rules

- One theme at a time
- Mode options only show curated combinations
- Glass and motion are global, never per-component props
- Motion modes are `full` | `reduced` | `off`; OS reduced-motion always wins over `full`
- Theme Studio authors custom packs; Theme Lab evaluates curated ones in context

---

## Theme Studio

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/theme-studio

Author a custom pack from a curated base — accent, radius, CSS export, and AI generate.

Free authoring starts here. Pick a curated base, set an accent seed and radius
preset, then watch a **full-width live dashboard** update as you edit. Open the
**bottom dock** (hover on desktop, tap on mobile) for Tokens, Generate and
Export. Download a drop-in CSS pack when ready. Some advanced token groups are
planned for Hewn Pro — [join the waitlist](/pro#waitlist).

<DocsThemeStudioFrame />

## Layout

| Area | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| **Dashboard** | Full-width Meridian Ops specimen (KPIs, chart, stream, crew) |
| **Bottom dock** | Collapsed summary; expands to authoring sheet |
| **Tokens** | Base pack, accent, radius, preview mode |
| **Generate** | AI prompt, CSS paste, or logo palette |
| **Pro** | Neutrals, semantics, density, glass, motion (coming soon) |
| **Export** | Download CSS, reset draft, Pro exporters |

Theme Lab evaluates **curated** packs across the docs shell. Theme Studio
authors a **custom** pack and proves it on an example dashboard.

## What’s free

- Base pack (Forest, Tide, Graphite, Dune, Clay, Ember)
- Accent seed (hex or `oklch(...)`) with contrast-safe foreground
- Radius presets (sharp / soft / rounded / pill)
- CSS export shaped like curated packs
- Draft saved in `localStorage` on this browser
- AI generate: offline heuristics always; optional BYOK OpenAI-compatible call

## AI generate

| Source | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| Prompt | Keyword + embedded-color heuristics; optional BYOK model JSON |
| CSS | Extract hex/`oklch` → accent + base pack suggestion |
| Logo | Client canvas palette sample → same proposal path |

Every proposal runs through the authoring engine (`normalize` + `derivePack`).
Invalid AI output falls back to offline heuristics. BYOK keys stay in
`localStorage` on this browser — never sent to Hewn servers.

## Pro authoring groups

Stub-gated in the Studio UI (engine already derives them):

| Group | Controls |
|-------|----------|
| Neutrals / surfaces | Surface lightness shift, chroma scale |
| Semantic colors | Danger seed |
| Shape / density | Compact / default / comfortable |
| Glass | Tint strength |
| Motion character | Snappy / balanced / soft |

Extra exporters (Tailwind `@theme`, Style Dictionary, Figma variables) are
planned for Hewn Pro beside the advanced authoring controls.

## Rules

- Engine clamps accents that fail WCAG AA and reports what changed
- Dashboard preview is scoped to the draft pack — Theme Lab still owns the docs shell
- Unsupported modes for a pack never appear (Dune/Clay light-only, Ember dark-only)
- No free-form CSS editing — guardrails are the product
- Generation is an accelerator; manual controls always work without a key

---

## Figma kit

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/themes/figma-kit

Import curated Hewn tokens into Figma via Tokens Studio.

The Figma kit is generated from the same curated packs as Theme Lab — six
identities, supported modes only, plus a sticker sheet for surfaces, button,
and input. No Figma plugin to maintain: Tokens Studio imports the JSON.

## Download

- [hewn.tokens.json](/figma/hewn.tokens.json) — Tokens Studio document
- [sticker-sheet.svg](/figma/sticker-sheet.svg) — visual reference sheet

Regenerate locally with `pnpm --filter @hewnui/themes generate`.

## Import into Figma

1. Install [Tokens Studio](https://tokens.studio/) in your Figma file
2. Open Tokens → Import → select `hewn.tokens.json`
3. Switch themes (for example `forest / light`) and create Figma variables
4. Paste or place `sticker-sheet.svg` as a starting sticker sheet

Full component parity in Figma is future scope — this kit covers variables and
the core surface vocabulary.

## CLI

```bash
hewn theme export
```

Prints paths and import notes (groundwork). Studio Pro exporters can also emit
a Tokens Studio document for a single authored pack.

---

## MCP

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/mcp

Local stdio MCP server for Hewn registry and AI schema.

`@hewnui/mcp` exposes a read-only Model Context Protocol server over stdio.
AI coding tools can list and inspect free components without scraping the docs
site.

The package is **private for the 0.1.0 release** and is not published to npm yet.

## Run

{/* Install command strings: packages/docs-metadata/src/distribution.ts */}

From the monorepo (after `pnpm generate` so registry + AI JSON exist) —
contributors only:

```bash
pnpm --filter @hewnui/mcp build
node packages/mcp/dist/cli.js
```

Set `HEWN_ROOT` if the server cannot find the workspace root.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `list_components` | Registry items |
| `search_components` | Substring search |
| `get_component` | Registry row + AI schema JSON |
| `get_install_command` | npm + CLI install strings |
| `get_theme` | Curated packs (or one pack by id) |
| `get_tokens` | Tokens for a component or theme pack |

## Cursor example

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hewn": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["packages/mcp/dist/cli.js"],
      "env": {
        "HEWN_ROOT": "/absolute/path/to/your-project"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Roadmap

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/roadmap

What ships free, what becomes Pro, and what comes next.

Hewn grows in phases. The free core stays free — Pro pays for
composition, not for primitives.

## Shipped

- **Foundation** — semantic OKLCH tokens, theme/mode/material/motion providers
- **Reference components** — Button, fields, Checkbox, Switch, Dialog, Select, Tabs, Table
- **Theme breadth** — six curated packs, tinted glass, Theme Lab
- **Rich free core** — DatePicker, Combobox, Menu, Toast, Drawer, Progress, Skeleton, DataTable
- **Distribution** — npm packages (`@hewnui/ui`, `@hewnui/motion`, `@hewnui/themes`), the `hewnui` CLI, the static registry, and the shadcn registry
- **Theme platform** — Theme Studio, Figma kit, charts, `/llms.txt`

### Next

- **AI schema v1** — `/ai/index.json`
- **`@hewnui/mcp`** — local stdio MCP
- **AI theme generation** — BYOK + offline heuristics in Theme Studio
- **Hewn Pro** — application blocks and pages — [join the waitlist](/pro#waitlist)

AI agents can start from [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) for a curated docs index, or
[`/ai/index.json`](/ai/index.json) for per-component machine-readable schema
(props, states, keyboard, tokens, install, examples).

## Free vs Pro

Free: all core components (including charts), six theme packs, glass, motion,
documentation, the curated Figma kit, the static registry, `/llms.txt`, and
the npm packages and CLI.

Pro (in development): application blocks and pages built on the free core —
[join the waitlist](/pro#waitlist). Advanced theme authoring and pack exporters
are planned for Pro.

Pro access is coming soon — GitHub sign-in will unlock it. Nothing to configure
today.

---

## Button

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/button

Pressable action control with variants, sizes, and loading state.

A concise action control built on React Aria. Press scale, focus rings, and
loading feedback follow the global motion setting.

<ButtonDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from "@hewnui/ui";

export function Example() {
  return <Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>;
}
```

## Variants

`primary`, `secondary`, `outline`, `ghost`, `glass`, `soft`, `glow`, `danger`, `danger-outline`, and `danger-soft`.

## Sizes

`sm` (40px min height), `md`, and `lg`.

## States

- **Loading** — sets `isDisabled`, shows a spinner glyph
- **Disabled** — reduces opacity and blocks pointer events
- **Focus** — visible ring using semantic `--kp-ring`

## Accessibility

- Native button semantics from React Aria
- Keyboard activation with Enter and Space
- Loading and disabled states expose `disabled` to assistive tech

---

## AreaChart

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/area-chart

Filled area chart for cumulative or volume trends.

AreaChart fills under each series with a translucent accent tint and draws the
same monotone stroke as LineChart.

<AreaChartDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { AreaChart } from "@hewnui/ui";

<AreaChart
  summary="Active users this month"
  series={[
    {
      id: "users",
      label: "Active",
      data: [
        { x: 1, y: 20 },
        { x: 2, y: 28 },
        { x: 3, y: 24 },
        { x: 4, y: 35 },
      ],
    },
  ]}
>
  <AreaChart.Tooltip />
</AreaChart>
```

## Accessibility

- The SVG is `role="img"` named by the required `summary`, which is also rendered as an `sr-only` caption
- Every point is focusable and labelled `"{series}: {x}, {y}"`, so the series can be read with Tab alone
- Focus opens the same tooltip as hover, and blur closes it
- Axis ticks and gridlines are `aria-hidden` — the summary carries the shape of the data
- `status="loading"` and `status="empty"` announce through `role="status"`; `status="error"` uses `role="alert"`

---

## Badge

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/badge

Status pill and tag indicator with solid, soft, outline, glass, and live dot variants.

Compact status indicator for tags, metadata, and active counts.

<BadgeDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@hewnui/ui";

export function Example() {
  return <Badge variant="soft" color="accent">New</Badge>;
}
```

## Variants

- `solid` — Bold filled background
- `soft` — Tinted surface background (default)
- `outline` — Bordered outline
- `glass` — Frosted glass material fill
- `dot` — Status dot indicator with accompanying label

## Colors

`accent`, `muted`, `danger`, `success`, and `warning`.

## Sizes

`sm`, `md` (default), and `lg`.

## Accessibility

- Badge renders a plain `<span>` with no implicit role, so it is announced as part of the
  surrounding text rather than as a widget
- The `dot` variant's indicator is `aria-hidden` — the label text has to carry the meaning
  ("Degraded", not colour alone)
- When a badge reflects live state, put it inside a `role="status"` region so changes are announced
- Pass `aria-label` through `...props` when the visible text is an abbreviation (`"P1"` → `"Priority 1"`)

---

## BarChart

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/bar-chart

Categorical bar chart with optional multi-series grouping.

BarChart maps categories on a band scale and groups series side-by-side.
Heights animate with a spring when motion is enabled.

<BarChartDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart } from "@hewnui/ui";

<BarChart
  summary="Tickets by status"
  series={[
    {
      id: "open",
      label: "Open",
      data: [
        { x: "Mon", y: 4 },
        { x: "Tue", y: 6 },
        { x: "Wed", y: 3 },
      ],
    },
  ]}
>
  <BarChart.Tooltip />
</BarChart>
```

## Accessibility

- The SVG is `role="img"` named by the required `summary`, which is also rendered as an `sr-only` caption
- Every bar is focusable and labelled `"{series}: {category}, {value}"`, so the data is reachable with Tab alone
- Focus opens the same tooltip as hover, and blur closes it
- Axis ticks and gridlines are `aria-hidden` — the summary carries the comparison
- `status="loading"` and `status="empty"` announce through `role="status"`; `status="error"` uses `role="alert"`

---

## DataTable

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/data-table

Advanced table powered by TanStack Table on Hewn surfaces.

DataTable keeps Hewn visuals while TanStack owns sorting state and
column definitions. Use the foundation Table for simpler static grids.

<DataTableDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { DataTable, type ColumnDef } from "@hewnui/ui";

const columns: ColumnDef<Row>[] = [
  { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
  { accessorKey: "score", header: "Score" },
];

<DataTable aria-label="Scores" columns={columns} data={rows} />
```

## Accessibility

- `aria-label` is a required prop, so the table is never unnamed
- React Aria grid semantics: arrow keys move between cells, Home/End jump along a row
- The first column is the row header, giving each row a name when a cell is read in isolation
- Sortable headers expose `aria-sort` (`none`, `ascending`, `descending`) and toggle with Enter or
  Space — the caret glyph is `aria-hidden`, so sort state never depends on seeing it
- Sorting is driven through React Aria's `sortDescriptor`, so the announcement stays in sync with
  the TanStack sort state

---

## DonutChart

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/donut-chart

Part-to-whole radial chart with a required summary and focusable slices.

DonutChart is the radial sibling of Area and Bar: same status frames, same
tooltip, slices you can Tab through.

## Usage

```tsx
import { DonutChart } from "@hewnui/ui";

<DonutChart
  summary="Traffic share last 24h"
  slices={[
    { id: "edge", label: "Edge", value: 62 },
    { id: "origin", label: "Origin", value: 38 },
  ]}
>
  <DonutChart.Tooltip />
</DonutChart>
```

## Preview

<DonutChartDemo />

## Accessibility

- The SVG is `role="img"` named by the required `summary`
- Every slice is focusable and labelled `"{name}: {value}"`
- Focus opens the same tooltip as hover
- `status="loading"` and empty (sum ≤ 0) use `role="status"`; `status="error"` uses `role="alert"`

---

## LineChart

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/line-chart

Multi-series line chart with optional tooltip.

LineChart plots one or more series with theme-token colors, grid/axis labels,
and draw-in motion. Use `LineChart.Tooltip` for point details.

<LineChartDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "@hewnui/ui";

<LineChart
  summary="Revenue by weekday"
  series={[
    {
      id: "rev",
      label: "Revenue",
      data: [
        { x: "Mon", y: 12 },
        { x: "Tue", y: 18 },
        { x: "Wed", y: 15 },
      ],
    },
  ]}
>
  <LineChart.Tooltip />
</LineChart>
```

## States

`loading`, `empty`, and `error` via the `status` prop (empty also when series
have no points).

## Accessibility

`role="img"` plus required `summary`. Points are keyboard-focusable when a
tooltip is used.

---

## Sparkline

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/sparkline

Compact inline trend line for dense data surfaces.

Sparkline is a minimal trend line for tables, cards, and dashboards. It uses
`role="img"` with a required summary and respects reduced motion.

<SparklineDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Sparkline } from "@hewnui/ui";

<Sparkline
  data={[4, 6, 5, 9, 7, 11]}
  summary="Signups over the last six weeks"
/>
```

## States

- `loading` — skeleton placeholder
- `empty` — dashed empty message (also when `data` is empty)
- `error` — alert message

## Accessibility

Provide a concrete `summary`. Prefer a surrounding visually-hidden data table
when the exact values matter.

---

## Table

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/table

Accessible data table foundation with sorting and empty states.

Lightweight table built on React Aria. Sorting stays client-side for the
foundation; TanStack-powered advanced tables come later.

<TableDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCell,
  TableColumn,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from "@hewnui/ui";

<Table aria-label="Team">
  <TableHeader>
    <TableColumn isRowHeader>Name</TableColumn>
    <TableColumn>Role</TableColumn>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody items={rows}>
    {(item) => (
      <TableRow id={item.id}>
        <TableCell>{item.name}</TableCell>
        <TableCell>{item.role}</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    )}
  </TableBody>
</Table>
```

## States

- Sorted columns via `allowsSorting` + `sortDescriptor`
- `TableEmpty` for zero-result layouts
- `TableLoading` for pending fetches

## Accessibility

- Grid semantics from React Aria Table
- Sortable column announcements
- Keyboard focus for rows and columns

## Compound API

`TableRoot.Header`, `TableRoot.Column`, `TableRoot.Body`, `TableRoot.Row`,
`TableRoot.Cell`, `TableRoot.Empty`, and `TableRoot.Loading` are also exported.

---

## DatePicker

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/date-picker

Accessible date field with calendar popover.

DatePicker wraps React Aria date segments and calendar navigation. Lives under
**Date and Time** in the component gallery.

<DatePickerDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from "@hewnui/ui";

export function Example() {
  return <DatePicker label="Ship date" />;
}
```

The field shows localized segments (year, month, day). Open the calendar from
the trailing button or by completing segment focus and activating the popover
trigger.

## States

- **Empty / valued** — segments show placeholders until filled
- **Required** — set `isRequired` when the date cannot be blank
- **Disabled** — set `isDisabled` to block segment editing and the calendar
- **Focus** — focused segments and calendar cells use a visible ring

## Keyboard

- `Tab` moves between the date group and the calendar button
- Arrow keys and typing edit the focused segment
- `Enter` or `Space` on the calendar button opens the popover
- Inside the grid, arrows move between days; `Enter` selects
- `Escape` closes the calendar and returns focus to the field
- `PageUp` / `PageDown` move by month when the grid is focused

## Accessibility

- Segmented date editing keeps each part individually reachable
- Calendar grid supports full keyboard navigation
- Localized formatting and calendar labels come from React Aria
- The field group is named by the `label` prop

---

## DateRangePicker

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/date-range-picker

Accessible start and end date fields with a range calendar popover and optional presets.

DateRangePicker wraps React Aria date segments and RangeCalendar navigation with
optional quick-select presets. Lives under **Date and Time** in the component
gallery.

<DateRangePickerDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { DateRangePicker } from "@hewnui/ui";

<DateRangePicker
  label="Travel dates"
  description="Inclusive stay"
  startName="start"
  endName="end"
/>
```

## Presets

Built-in presets cover Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, and This month. Pass
`showPresets={false}` to hide them, or supply a custom `presets` list.

```tsx
<DateRangePicker
  label="Report range"
  presets={["today", "last-7-days", "this-month"]}
/>
```

## Bounds and unavailable dates

```tsx
import { getLocalTimeZone, today } from "@internationalized/date";

const now = today(getLocalTimeZone());

<DateRangePicker
  label="Booking window"
  minValue={now}
  maxValue={now.add({ months: 3 })}
  isDateUnavailable={(date) => date.toDate(getLocalTimeZone()).getDay() === 0}
/>
```

## Accessibility

- Dual segmented date fields for start and end
- Range calendar grid keyboard navigation
- Localized formatting via React Aria
- Form submission through `startName` and `endName`

---

## Empty

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/empty

Status region for lists and tables with nothing to show.

Empty tells people the region is intentional, not broken. Pair it with an action
when they can populate it.

<EmptyDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button, Empty } from "@hewnui/ui";

<Empty title="No jobs" action={<Button>Queue deploy</Button>}>
  Routed work will land here.
</Empty>
```

## Accessibility

- Renders `role="status"` so a newly empty region is announced
- `title` is the name of the state; supporting copy is optional
- Keep the action a real control (Button, Link) — do not put the only next step in placeholder art

---

## Progress

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/progress

Determinate and indeterminate progress feedback.

Progress uses React Aria progressbar semantics and tabular percentages.

<ProgressDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@hewnui/ui";

<Progress label="Bundle sync" value={47} />
```

## Accessibility

- React Aria progressbar semantics: `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax` track
  `value`, `minValue`, and `maxValue`
- `label` renders a real `<Label>` tied to the bar — pass one whenever the bar is not already
  described by nearby text
- `isIndeterminate` drops the numeric value so assistive tech announces "busy" rather than a
  misleading percentage
- The percentage readout uses tabular numerals so it does not jitter while counting
- The indeterminate sweep falls back to a pulse under `prefers-reduced-motion`

---

## Skeleton

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/skeleton

Placeholder blocks for loading layouts.

Skeleton is a lightweight pulse surface. Compose multiple blocks to match
content geometry.

<SkeletonDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@hewnui/ui";

<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
```

## Accessibility

- Skeleton is `aria-hidden` — it is decorative geometry, never an announcement
- Because it is silent, pair it with a live region so screen reader users learn that content is
  loading:

```tsx
<div role="status" aria-live="polite">
  <span className="sr-only">Loading rows…</span>
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-2/3" />
</div>
```

- Remove the live region once the real content lands, or the announcement repeats
- The pulse is a CSS animation and is suppressed by `prefers-reduced-motion`

---

## Spinner

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/spinner

Indeterminate loading indicator for inline and status feedback.

Spinner is a decorative indeterminate indicator. It renders `aria-hidden` —
announce loading through the surrounding region or control text instead.

<SpinnerDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@hewnui/ui";

<Spinner />
```

## Sizing and color

Spinner is a 1rem square by default and inherits `currentColor`, so it takes
the color of whatever it sits inside. Override either with `className`:

```tsx
<Spinner className="size-6" />
<Spinner className="size-8 text-accent" />
```

## Inside a button

`Button` renders a Spinner for you when `isLoading` is set — you do not need to
compose one yourself:

```tsx
<Button isLoading>Saving</Button>
```

## Accessibility

Spinner is `aria-hidden` by design. A spinning shape carries no meaning for a
screen reader, so it is never announced on its own — the surrounding context
has to do that work.

- Pair it with a live region when the spinner is the only signal that something
  is happening:

```tsx
<p role="status">
  <Spinner />
  Loading results
</p>
```

- Inside `Button`, the accessible name already conveys state and the button is
  disabled while loading — no extra live region is needed.
- Do not add `role="status"` or `aria-label` to Spinner itself. Announce the
  state on the region that owns it, or the message is read out of context.
- Motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` in CSS: the rotation stops
  and the ring resolves to a static, dimmed indicator. No JavaScript involved,
  so it works before hydration.

---

## Toast

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/toast

Motion-aware notification stack with global provider.

Toasts stack from the corner with a tone well, lifetime bar, and dismiss
control. Tones: `default`, `success`, `danger`, `warning`, and `info`.
Reduced motion softens entrance and freezes the lifetime bar.

<ToastDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button, ToastProvider, useToast } from "@hewnui/ui";

function Notify() {
  const { toast } = useToast();
  return (
    <Button
      onPress={() =>
        toast({ title: "Draft saved", tone: "success" })
      }
    >
      Notify
    </Button>
  );
}
```

Wrap the app with `ToastProvider` once — already included in the docs shell.

## Tones

| Tone | Use |
|------|-----|
| `default` | Neutral status |
| `success` | Completed save or sync |
| `danger` | Failure that needs attention |
| `warning` | Soft risk or quota pressure |
| `info` | Tip or non-blocking guidance |

## Accessibility

- `danger` toasts render `role="alert"` with `aria-live="assertive"`; every other tone uses
  `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`, so routine confirmations never interrupt
- The dismiss control is a real button labelled "Dismiss notification"
- The countdown bar is `aria-hidden` and freezes when motion is off
- Toasts auto-dismiss after 4200ms by default. Raise `duration` for longer messages, and do not
  put an action's only affordance inside a toast — the timer does not pause on hover or focus.

<Callout type="warn">
  A toast is the wrong home for anything the user must act on. For blocking errors or decisions,
  use an inline message or a Dialog, which stay on screen until dismissed.
</Callout>

---

## Checkbox

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/checkbox

Binary selection control with motion-aware check feedback.

Checkbox uses React Aria selection behavior and a compact indicator. When motion
is on, the check mark springs in; reduced motion keeps an instant mark.

<CheckboxDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@hewnui/ui";

export function Example() {
  return <Checkbox defaultSelected>Email product updates</Checkbox>;
}
```

Use `isSelected` / `onChange` for controlled forms. Pair related options with
`CheckboxGroup` when they share one label and validation message.

## States

- **Selected / unselected** — animated check mark when motion is enabled
- **Indeterminate** — set `isIndeterminate` for partial selection parents
- **Invalid** — set `isInvalid` to mark a required unchecked choice
- **Disabled** — reduces opacity and blocks activation
- **Pressed** — scale feedback on the indicator when motion is on
- **Focus** — ring on the indicator via `--kp-ring`

## Keyboard

- `Tab` moves focus to the checkbox
- `Space` toggles selection
- Disabled checkboxes are not focusable

## Accessibility

- Native checkbox role and checked state from React Aria
- Indeterminate is exposed to assistive tech separately from checked
- Keep the label as children so the hit target includes the text
- Visible focus ring stays on the indicator box

Wraps React Aria CheckboxGroup around Hewn `Checkbox` items. Use when

- Description helper text

- Each checkbox keeps its own accessible name
- Keyboard and screen reader behavior from React Aria

- Drop target highlight (solid accent edge + press scale)
- Selected file list with remove actions

Under the global **glass** material, the zone and file rows pick up tinted frost

## Form

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/form

Accessible form container for native and custom field validation.

Thin wrapper around React Aria Form. Compose Hewn fields inside and use
native constraint validation or `validationErrors` for server feedback.

<FormDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button, Form, TextField } from "@hewnui/ui";

<Form onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
  <TextField label="Email" name="email" type="email" isRequired />
  <Button type="submit">Continue</Button>
</Form>
```

## Notes

- No React Hook Form or Formik dependency
- Fields keep their own labels, descriptions, and errors
- Use `validationErrors` for server-side messages keyed by field name

## Accessibility

- Landmark `form` role when labeled
- Focus moves to the first invalid field on failed submit

## Switch

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/switch

Immediate on/off control for preferences and modes.

Switch is for instant settings, not delayed form commits. The track and thumb
use CSS transforms, and press scale follows the global motion setting.

<SwitchDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Switch } from "@hewnui/ui";

export function Example() {
  return <Switch defaultSelected>Enable motion</Switch>;
}
```

Controlled usage takes `isSelected` with `onChange`. Uncontrolled usage prefers
`defaultSelected`.

## States

- **Selected / unselected** — thumb travels along the track
- **Disabled** — reduces opacity and blocks pointer and keyboard activation
- **Focus** — visible ring on the track via `--kp-ring`
- **Pressed** — scale feedback when motion is enabled

## Keyboard

- `Tab` moves focus to the switch
- `Space` toggles the value
- Disabled switches are skipped in the tab order

## Accessibility

- Exposes the native `switch` role from React Aria
- The label text is associated with the control; keep meaningful children
- Selected state is announced to assistive tech
- Focus-visible ring stays on the track, not the label text

## Card

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/card

Elevated panel with optional header, body, and footer.

  <Card.Footer>vs prior window</Card.Footer>

## Breadcrumbs

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/breadcrumbs

Hierarchical trail linking ancestors to the current page.

Compound `Breadcrumbs` and `Breadcrumb` built on React Aria. Ancestor crumbs
render as links; the current page renders as plain text with
`aria-current="page"`.

<BreadcrumbsDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb, Breadcrumbs } from "@hewnui/ui";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumbs>
      <Breadcrumb href="/docs">Docs</Breadcrumb>
      <Breadcrumb href="/docs/components">Components</Breadcrumb>
      <Breadcrumb>Button</Breadcrumb>
    </Breadcrumbs>
  );
}
```

Omit `href` (or set `isCurrent`) on the final crumb. Set `aria-label` on
`Breadcrumbs` when the page has more than one navigation landmark.

## States

- **Current** — last crumb without `href`, announced as the current page
- **Disabled** — `isDisabled` on `Breadcrumbs` mutes the whole trail
- **Focus** — link crumbs show a focus ring on keyboard focus

## Keyboard

- `Tab` moves through ancestor links
- `Enter` activates the focused ancestor
- The current page crumb is not a link and is skipped as a tab stop
- Disabled trails remove all crumbs from the tab order

## Accessibility

- Renders a navigation landmark; provide `aria-label` when needed
- Current page is marked with `aria-current="page"`
- Separators are presentational and hidden from the accessibility tree
- Keep crumb labels short and unique within the trail

---

## Link

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/link

Accessible navigation link with accent, muted, and underline variants.

Styled React Aria Link for in-app and external navigation. Prefer Link over raw
anchors so focus, press, and disabled states stay consistent with the rest of
the system.

<LinkDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Link } from "@hewnui/ui";

export function Example() {
  return <Link href="/docs/getting-started">Getting started</Link>;
}
```

Pass `href` for navigation. For external destinations, React Aria still owns
keyboard and focus behavior; add `target` / `rel` only when you need them.

## Variants

`accent` (default), `muted`, and `underline`.

## States

- **Hover / press** — color shift and press scale when motion is on
- **Focus** — visible ring using semantic `--kp-ring`
- **Disabled** — set `isDisabled` to block navigation and mute the style

## Keyboard

- `Tab` moves focus to the link
- `Enter` activates navigation
- Disabled links are removed from the tab order

## Accessibility

- Native link semantics from React Aria
- Press scale feedback does not replace a clear focus ring
- Disabled state exposes `aria-disabled` and prevents activation
- Prefer descriptive link text over “click here”

Accessible page navigation with numbered pages, ellipsis, and optional links.

Pagination is a navigation landmark with previous/next controls, numbered pages,

- Previous/next disabled at the ends
- Optional fully disabled pager

## Accessibility

- `nav` landmark with an accessible name
- Keyboard focusable controls activated with Enter or Space
- Page numbers use tabular numerals
- Ellipsis markers are presentational

## Stepper

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/stepper

Multi-step progress indicator with horizontal and vertical orientations.

Stepper tracks wizard progress with complete, current, upcoming, error, and
optional states. Pair it with `useStepper` for controlled flows.

<StepperDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Stepper, StepperStep, useStepper } from "@hewnui/ui";

const { currentIndex, goTo, next, previous } = useStepper({ count: 3 });

  <StepperStep description="Name and owners">Account</StepperStep>
  <StepperStep>Details</StepperStep>
  <StepperStep isOptional>Review</StepperStep>
</Stepper>
```

## States

- Complete, current, upcoming (derived or explicit)
- Error — alert glyph in the indicator
- Optional — dashed indicator + Optional label

## Accessibility

- Navigation landmark with an accessible name
- Current step exposes `aria-current="step"`
- Indicators are presentational; titles provide the accessible name
- Clickable completed steps are real buttons with 40×40 indicators and press scale
- Connectors are `aria-hidden`

## CommandPalette

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/command-palette

Modal ⌘K command finder with grouped actions, shortcuts, and async loading.

CommandPalette pairs a dialog trigger with React Aria Autocomplete and Menu.
Filter grouped commands, show shortcut hints, and wire an optional global hotkey.

<CommandPaletteDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  CommandPalette,
  CommandPaletteGroup,
  CommandPaletteInput,
  CommandPaletteItem,
  CommandPaletteList,
  CommandPaletteTrigger,
  useCommandPaletteHotkey,
} from "@hewnui/ui";

const [isOpen, setOpen] = useState(false);
useCommandPaletteHotkey({ onOpenChange: setOpen });

<CommandPaletteTrigger isOpen={isOpen} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <Button>Commands</Button>
  <CommandPalette>
    <CommandPaletteInput />
    <CommandPaletteList>
      <CommandPaletteGroup heading="Actions">
        <CommandPaletteItem id="new" shortcut="⌘N" textValue="New file">
          New file
        </CommandPaletteItem>
      </CommandPaletteGroup>
    </CommandPaletteList>
  </CommandPalette>
</CommandPaletteTrigger>
```

## States

- Loading — `CommandPaletteList isLoading` shows a polite status with spinner
- Empty — filtered Menu `renderEmptyState` via `emptyLabel`
- Disabled — `CommandPaletteItem isDisabled`

## Accessibility

- Dialog role with an accessible name; focus moves into the search field on open
- Escape and outside click dismiss; focus returns to the trigger
- Arrow keys move between commands; Enter activates; typeahead filtering via Autocomplete
- Shortcut hints use the `Keyboard` element; icons are presentational
- Reduced motion: enter/exit transitions fall back with `motion-reduce`

## Docs search note

The docs site still uses Fumadocs search. CommandPalette could wrap that surface later
(same trigger + Autocomplete pattern) without changing this component’s API — not
refactored in this release.

---

## Dialog

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/dialog

Modal surface for confirmations and focused tasks.

Dialog pairs a trigger with a dismissible modal. Content uses compound parts
for title, body, and actions.

<DialogDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  Dialog,
  DialogActions,
  DialogBody,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@hewnui/ui";

<DialogTrigger>
  <Button>Open</Button>
  <Dialog title="Confirm">
    <DialogBody>Archive this draft?</DialogBody>
    <DialogActions>
      <Button variant="secondary" slot="close">Cancel</Button>
      <Button slot="close">Confirm</Button>
    </DialogActions>
  </Dialog>
</DialogTrigger>
```

## Accessibility

- Dialog role and labeled title
- Escape and outside click dismiss
- Focus moves into the modal while open

---

## Drawer

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/drawer

Side panel overlay for filters and dense tools.

Drawer docks to the left or right edge for filters and dense tools. Escape,
overlay click, and the header close button all dismiss it while restoring focus
to the trigger.

<DrawerDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button, Drawer, DrawerTrigger } from "@hewnui/ui";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <DrawerTrigger>
      <Button>Filters</Button>
      <Drawer title="Filters" side="right">
        Content
      </Drawer>
    </DrawerTrigger>
  );
}
```

Wrap the trigger and panel in `DrawerTrigger`. Control open state with `isOpen`
and `onOpenChange` when the host page owns the lifecycle.

## Variants

`side="right"` (default) and `side="left"`. Title is required so the dialog has
an accessible name.

## States

- **Closed / open** — focus moves into the panel while open
- **Dismissing** — Escape, overlay press, and the close button all close it
- **Focus** — close control and in-panel controls keep visible focus rings

## Keyboard

- Activate the trigger with `Enter` or `Space`
- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` cycle focus inside the open drawer
- `Escape` dismisses and returns focus to the trigger
- The header close button is reachable by keyboard and named “Close drawer”

## Accessibility

- Dialog semantics with a titled heading from the `title` prop
- Overlay is dismissible; outside click and Escape both close when enabled
- Focus is trapped in the panel while open
- Close glyph is decorative; the button carries an accessible name

---

## Menu

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/menu

Action menu triggered from a button.

Use Menu for compact action lists. Separators group destructive choices.

<MenuDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Menu, MenuButton, MenuItem, MenuTrigger } from "@hewnui/ui";

<MenuTrigger>
  <MenuButton>Actions</MenuButton>
  <Menu>
    <MenuItem id="edit">Edit</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="archive">Archive</MenuItem>
  </Menu>
</MenuTrigger>
```

## Accessibility

- `MenuTrigger` wires `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded` onto the button and moves focus into the
  menu when it opens
- Arrow keys move between items, Home/End jump to the ends, and typeahead matches by first letters
- Enter or Space fires `onAction`; Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger
- Items marked `isDisabled` are exposed as disabled and cannot be activated
- `MenuSeparator` renders `role="separator"` so groups are announced as distinct

## Popover

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/popover

Anchored content panel for short explanations without a modal layer.

DialogTrigger + Popover pattern for lightweight overlays. Heavier confirmations
still belong in Dialog.

<PopoverDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  Popover,
  PopoverBody,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@hewnui/ui";

<PopoverTrigger>
  <Button>Details</Button>
  <Popover>
    <PopoverTitle>Latency</PopoverTitle>
    <PopoverBody>Median response is 47.2ms.</PopoverBody>
  </Popover>
</PopoverTrigger>
```

## Accessibility

- Opens as a dialog for focus management
- Esc and outside click dismiss
- Title uses the dialog heading slot

## Tooltip

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/tooltip

Short contextual hint anchored to a trigger on hover or focus.

Built on React Aria TooltipTrigger and Tooltip. Prefer for brief labels; use
Popover when the content needs a title or actions.

<TooltipDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button, Tooltip, TooltipTrigger } from "@hewnui/ui";

<TooltipTrigger>
  <Button>Help</Button>
  <Tooltip>Keyboard shortcut</Tooltip>
</TooltipTrigger>
```

## Placement

Defaults to `top`. Pass `placement` for other overlay sides.

## Accessibility

- Appears on hover and keyboard focus
- Exposed with `role="tooltip"`
- Delay defaults to 400ms; demos often use a shorter delay

## ColorPicker

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/color-picker

Composable color picker with area, hue and alpha sliders, hex field, and swatch presets.

ColorPicker synchronizes React Aria ColorArea, ColorSlider, ColorField, and
swatch presets. Returns a hex string and can show a read-only OKLCH readout.
Lives under **Pickers** in the component gallery.

<ColorPickerDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { ColorPicker } from "@hewnui/ui";

<ColorPicker label="Brand accent" defaultValue="#1a6b4a" />
```

## Inline panel

```tsx
<ColorPicker
  label="Fill color"
  variant="inline"
  showOklch
  description="Hex is editable; OKLCH is display-only."
/>
```

## Presets and alpha

```tsx
<ColorPicker
  label="Opaque only"
  showAlpha={false}
  presets={["#1a6b4a", "#0f766e", "#b45309", "#334155"]}
/>
```

## Accessibility

- Labeled saturation/brightness area, hue slider, and alpha slider
- Hex field for precise entry
- Keyboard navigation across area, sliders, field, and swatches
- Hidden `name` input for HTML form submission

## Combobox

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/combobox

Searchable single-select built on React Aria ComboBox.

Combobox keeps typing and list filtering in one field. Lives under **Pickers**
in the component gallery.

<ComboboxDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Combobox, ComboboxItem } from "@hewnui/ui";

<Combobox label="City" defaultSelectedKey="lisbon">
  <ComboboxItem id="lisbon">Lisbon</ComboboxItem>
  <ComboboxItem id="porto">Porto</ComboboxItem>
</Combobox>
```

## Accessibility

- The input carries `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded` and is wired to the listbox popover
- `label` renders a real `<Label>` bound to the input — pass `aria-label` instead only when the
  field is already labelled by adjacent text
- Arrow keys move through options, Enter selects the focused option, Escape closes the popover
- The toggle button is labelled by React Aria, so the ▾ glyph is never read aloud
- Pass `textValue` on `ComboboxItem` when its children are not plain text, so typeahead and
  announcements still have something to say

---

## Select

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/select

Single-select control with popover listbox.

Select keeps a concise labeled trigger while list items stay composable. Lives
under **Pickers** in the component gallery.

<SelectDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { Select, SelectItem } from "@hewnui/ui";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Select label="Theme pack" defaultSelectedKey="forest">
      <SelectItem id="forest">Forest</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem id="tide">Tide</SelectItem>
    </Select>
  );
}
```

Use `selectedKey` / `onSelectionChange` for controlled value. Pass `textValue`
on `SelectItem` when children are not plain text so typeahead still works.

## Variants

`outline` (default), `filled`, `flushed`, and `glass`. Under the global glass
material, boxed variants pick up tinted frost; `flushed` stays underline-only.

## States

- **Placeholder** — shown until a key is selected
- **Disabled** — `isDisabled` mutes the trigger and blocks opening
- **Invalid / required** — `isInvalid` and `isRequired` for form validation
- **Focus** — ring on the trigger; list items highlight on keyboard focus

## Keyboard

- `Tab` focuses the trigger
- `Enter`, `Space`, or `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` opens the listbox
- Arrow keys move through options; typeahead jumps by printable characters
- `Enter` selects the focused option; `Escape` closes without changing value
- Disabled selects are skipped in the tab order

## Accessibility

- Trigger uses button/combobox semantics from React Aria with `aria-expanded`
- `label` renders a real field label bound to the trigger
- Selected option is announced when the popover closes
- Listbox items expose selected and disabled states to assistive tech

---

## TagField

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/components/tag-field

Filterable multi-select that shows selections as removable tags.

TagField (also exported as `MultiSelect`) combines React Aria ComboBox
multi-select with a TagGroup of removable chips. Lives under **Pickers** in the
component gallery.

<TagFieldDemo />

## Usage

```tsx
import { TagField, TagFieldItem } from "@hewnui/ui";

<TagField label="Skills" defaultValue={["react"]} maxSelections={3} name="skills">
  <TagFieldItem id="react">React</TagFieldItem>
  <TagFieldItem id="svelte">Svelte</TagFieldItem>
  <TagFieldItem id="vue" isDisabled>
    Vue
  </TagFieldItem>
</TagField>
```

`MultiSelect` / `MultiSelectItem` are aliases for the same API.

## States

- Empty tag list (optional `emptyLabel`)
- Empty filtered list (`listEmptyLabel`)
- Disabled field and disabled items
- Invalid + `errorMessage`
- Maximum selections reached (announced live)

## Accessibility

- Combobox + listbox semantics from React Aria
- Selected values render in a TagGroup grid with remove buttons
- Backspace on an empty input removes the last tag
- Arrow keys move between tags; Delete/remove clears the focused tag
- Screen readers hear selection count and max-selection announcements

## CLI lint

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/cli-lint

Static checks for Hewn tokens, contrast, motion, and overlay a11y.

`hewn lint` walks your project (and this monorepo in CI) for design-system
guarantees. It uses the TypeScript compiler API when available and prints
`file:line:column` findings with rule ids.

```bash
npx hewnui@latest lint
npx hewnui@latest lint src/components --json
npx hewnui@latest lint --fix
```

Exit code is `1` when any **error**-severity finding remains. Warnings do not
fail the process.

## Configuration

Extend `hewn.json` (created by `hewn init`):

```json
{
  "root": "components/hewn",
  "tsx": true,
  "lint": {
    "include": ["**/*.{ts,tsx,css}"],
    "ignore": ["**/*.test.*", "**/dist/**"],
    "themes": ["**/node_modules/@hewnui/themes/**/*.css"],
    "rules": {
      "tokens-only": "error",
      "aa-contrast": "error",
      "reduced-motion": "error",
      "labelled-overlays": "error",
      "destructive-confirms": "warn"
    }
  }
}
```

Set a rule to `"off"` to disable it. `ignore` globs apply to source files and
theme CSS used by `aa-contrast`.

## Rule reference

### `tokens-only`

Flags raw colour literals in components — hex, `rgb`/`hsl`/`oklch`/`oklab`, and
Tailwind arbitrary colours such as `bg-[#…]`. Prefer semantic tokens
(`var(--kp-foreground)`, `bg-accent`, …).

Allowlisted: Hewn token definitions (`--kp-*`), fragment `href="#…"`
anchors, and neutral black/white OKLCH recipes used for shadows and glass
refraction (`oklch(0 0 0 / α)`, `oklch(1 0 0 / α)`).

### `aa-contrast`

Reads theme pack CSS (or paths in `lint.themes`) and checks semantic pairs:

| Pair | Minimum |
|------|---------|
| `--kp-foreground` on `--kp-background` / `--kp-surface` | 4.5:1 text |
| `--kp-accent-foreground` on `--kp-accent` | 4.5:1 text |
| `--kp-muted-foreground` on `--kp-background` / `--kp-muted` | 3:1 large/UI |
| `--kp-accent` / `--kp-danger` on `--kp-background` | 3:1 UI |

Contrast math converts OKLCH → sRGB → WCAG relative luminance.

### `reduced-motion`

Flags `transition-all` / `transition: all`, and Motion usage
(`motion/react` or `framer-motion`) without a statically detectable
reduced-motion path (`useReducedMotion`, `useMotionMode`, `motionEnabled`,
`MotionConfig`, or `prefers-reduced-motion`).

`--fix` rewrites `transition-all` to an explicit property list
(`color`, `background-color`, `border-color`, `opacity`, `transform`,
`box-shadow`).

### `labelled-overlays`

Flags `Dialog` / `Modal` / `Sheet` / `Drawer` usages without an accessible
name (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `title` prop, or `Heading` slot).
Passthrough composition shells (`<Dialog>{children}</Dialog>`) are skipped.
Popovers are not flagged — they typically inherit the trigger name.

### `destructive-confirms` (warning)

Heuristic: `Button` with a danger/destructive variant whose press handler or
label looks delete-like (`delete`, `remove`, …) without a confirm pattern
(`Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, `window.confirm`, …) in the same file.

## JSON output

```bash
npx hewnui@latest lint --json
```

```json
{
  "errorCount": 1,
  "warnCount": 0,
  "fixed": 0,
  "findings": [
    {
      "ruleId": "tokens-only",
      "severity": "error",
      "message": "Raw colour literal — use a semantic token…",
      "file": "src/Button.tsx",
      "line": 12,
      "column": 18
    }
  ]
}
```

## Getting started

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/getting-started

Install from npm, then wire providers and Tailwind CSS v4.

{/* Install command strings: packages/docs-metadata/src/distribution.ts (PACKAGES_PUBLISHED). */}

Hewn is a motion-native React component library built on React Aria,
Tailwind CSS v4, and Motion. Install the packages from npm, copy components
into your project with the CLI, or fetch component JSON from the [live
registry](https://hewnui.dev/r/index.free.json).

## Install

Install the components and theme layers from npm:

```bash
pnpm add @hewnui/ui @hewnui/themes
```

Or pull a component's source straight from the registry:

```bash
curl -s https://hewnui.dev/r/button.json
```

Peer dependencies (needed whether you install from npm or own the source):

```bash
pnpm add react react-dom react-aria-components motion
```

| Peer | Supported range |
|------|-----------------|
| `react` | `^19.2.7` |
| `react-dom` | `^19.2.7` |
| `react-aria-components` | `^1.19.0` |
| `motion` | `^12.42.2` |

Prefer to own the source? Run `npx hewnui@latest init`, then
`npx hewnui@latest add button` — see the [CLI reference](/docs/cli).

## Tailwind CSS v4

Hewn targets Tailwind v4, which is configured in CSS rather than a
`tailwind.config.js`. Import Tailwind and the theme layers in your global
stylesheet. These resolve from the `@hewnui/themes` package installed
above.

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@import "@hewnui/themes/tokens.css";
@import "@hewnui/themes/radius.css";
@import "@hewnui/themes/glass.css";
@import "@hewnui/themes/glass-buttons.css";
```

`tokens.css` is required — it defines the semantic `--kp-*` custom properties
every component reads. The rest are opt-in: `radius.css` powers the global
radius scale, and the two `glass` layers are only needed if you use the tinted
glass material.

Tailwind v4 only generates classes it can see, so point `@source` at the
installed package or it will strip the component styles:

```css
@source "../node_modules/@hewnui/ui/dist/**/*.js";
```

If you copied source instead, point `@source` at your component root (for
example `components/hewn`) — or omit it entirely when the files already
sit inside your default content paths.

<Callout type="warn">
  Do not configure the Tailwind v3 PostCSS plugin. Hewn requires
  `@tailwindcss/postcss`; the legacy plugin will not resolve the `@import`
  layers above.
</Callout>

## Providers

Wrap your app once, as high as possible. Each provider owns one global concern
and writes a `data-*` attribute on `<html>` that the token layers respond to.

```tsx
"use client";

import {
  MaterialProvider,
  MotionProvider,
  RadiusProvider,
  ThemeProvider,
  ToastProvider,
} from "@hewnui/ui";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

export function Providers({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="forest" defaultMode="light">
      <MaterialProvider defaultMaterial="solid">
        <RadiusProvider defaultRadius="soft">
          <MotionProvider defaultMotion="full">
            <ToastProvider>{children}</ToastProvider>
          </MotionProvider>
        </RadiusProvider>
      </MaterialProvider>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

| Provider | Controls | Values |
|----------|----------|--------|
| `ThemeProvider` | Active pack and mode | `forest`, `tide`, `graphite`, `dune`, `clay`, `ember` |
| `MaterialProvider` | Global surface material | `solid`, `glass` |
| `RadiusProvider` | Global radius scale | `sharp`, `soft`, `rounded`, `pill` |
| `MotionProvider` | Global motion mode | `full`, `reduced`, `off` |
| `ToastProvider` | Toast queue and region | — |

Only `ThemeProvider` is strictly required. Add the others when you want global
control over material, radius, motion, or toasts.

Not every pack supports both modes — Dune and Clay are light-only, Ember is
dark-only, and Forest, Tide, and Graphite support both. Requesting an
unsupported mode falls back to the pack's first allowed mode. See
[Themes](/docs/themes) for the full matrix.

<Callout>
  `MotionProvider` never overrides the OS. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
  caps the effective mode at `reduced` — a `full` preference cannot win. See
  [Motion](/docs/motion) for tokens and the transform-only contract.
</Callout>

## First component

```tsx
import { Button } from "@hewnui/ui";

export function Example() {
  return <Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>;
}
```

## Next steps

- [Browse the components](/docs/components) — every free component with live examples
- [Theme Lab](/docs/theme-lab) — preview a theme across every state and variant
- [Theme Studio](/docs/theme-studio) — author your own pack from an accent seed

## shadcn CLI

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/shadcn

Install Hewn through the shadcn CLI and MCP with a namespaced registry.

Hewn publishes a **shadcn-schema** registry alongside the native
Hewn CLI registry. Use it when you already standardize on
`components.json`, the shadcn CLI, or the shadcn MCP.

The native `hewn` CLI and `/r/*.json` payloads are unchanged. The shadcn
output lives at `/r/shadcn/` and is generated from the same `packages/ui`
source.

## Configure the namespace

Add `@hewnui` to `components.json` under `registries`. The URL always
comes from this deployment’s site origin — do not hard-code a domain:

<DocsShadcnRegistrySnippet />

Or register it with the CLI:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @hewnui=<site-url>/r/shadcn/{name}.json
```

Replace `<site-url>` with the origin shown above (or your preview URL).

Point the UI alias at a folder that can hold nested component packages (the
registry installs into `@ui/<name>/…` and shared `@ui/utils`, `@ui/providers`.
Theme CSS lands under `@/components/hewn/theme/…`, or use the npm package):

```json
{
  "aliases": {
    "ui": "@/components/hewn"
  }
}
```

## Install components

<DocsShadcnAddExample />

Shared foundation items resolve automatically via `registryDependencies`:

| Item | Type | Role |
|------|------|------|
| `utils` | `registry:lib` | `cn` helper |
| `providers` | `registry:lib` | theme / material / radius / motion providers |
| `styles` | `registry:lib` | shared field and overlay classes |
| `motion-presets` | `registry:lib` | Motion springs + LazyMotion loader |
| `tokens` | `registry:theme` | pack CSS, radius, glass, `@theme` bridge |

npm packages listed on each item (`react-aria-components`, `motion`,
`@tanstack/react-table`, …) are installed by the shadcn CLI.

## Wire CSS and providers

After the first install, import the theme layer in your global CSS (Tailwind
v4):

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@hewnui/themes/tokens.css";
@import "@hewnui/themes/radius.css";
```

Or, after the `tokens` registry item is copied locally:

```css
@import "../components/hewn/theme/tokens.css";
@import "../components/hewn/theme/radius.css";
```

Wrap the app with the copied providers (theme is required). Import each file
from `@/components/hewn/providers/`:

```tsx
import { ThemeProvider } from "@/components/hewn/providers/theme-provider";
import { MaterialProvider } from "@/components/hewn/providers/material-provider";
import { RadiusProvider } from "@/components/hewn/providers/radius-provider";
import { MotionProvider } from "@/components/hewn/providers/motion-provider";
```

## shadcn MCP

With the same `components.json` registries entry, the shadcn MCP can list and
inspect `@hewnui/*` items. Catalog discovery uses
`/r/shadcn/registry.json`; individual items use `/r/shadcn/{name}.json`.

## Native CLI still available

Prefer copy-via-Hewn tooling? Use [`hewn` CLI](/docs/cli) and the
original `/r/*.json` registry — both channels stay in sync from
`packages/ui`.

---

## Theme export

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/themes/export

Download DESIGN.md, DTCG tokens, Tailwind v4 @theme, and agent skills for every curated pack.

Every curated Hewn theme can be exported in four free formats — from Theme
Lab for the active pack, from Theme Studio for a draft, or as static files under
`/themes/{pack}/`.

## Formats

| Format | File | Use |
|--------|------|-----|
| Design brief | `DESIGN.md` | Human- and AI-readable palette, typography, radius, motion, do/don't |
| DTCG tokens | `tokens.dtcg.json` | W3C Design Tokens (`$value` / `$type`) with light and dark modes |
| Tailwind v4 | `theme.css` | `@theme` block plus mode remaps |
| Agent skill | `SKILL.md` | Cursor-style skill telling agents how to apply the theme |

All six packs are free. Advanced Studio exporters (Style Dictionary, Figma
variables) remain structured for a future unlock and are separate from these
formats.

## Static paths

Files are generated at build time. Replace `{pack}` with `forest`, `tide`,
`graphite`, `dune`, `clay`, or `ember`:

- [`/themes/{pack}/DESIGN.md`](/themes/forest/DESIGN.md)
- [`/themes/{pack}/tokens.dtcg.json`](/themes/forest/tokens.dtcg.json)
- [`/themes/{pack}/theme.css`](/themes/forest/theme.css)
- [`/themes/{pack}/SKILL.md`](/themes/forest/SKILL.md)
- [`/themes/index.json`](/themes/index.json) — catalog of packs and formats

Regenerate with `pnpm --filter @hewnui/themes generate` (also runs during
`pnpm generate` / docs build).

## Theme Lab

Open [Theme Lab](/docs/theme-lab), pick a pack in the appearance controls, then
use **Download** or **Copy** on each format. Buttons are keyboard-focusable with
visible labels and live regions for copy confirmation.

## Theme Studio

Author a custom accent pack in [Theme Studio](/docs/theme-studio), open the
**Export** tab, and download the same four formats for your draft (plus drop-in
pack CSS).

## Engine

Exporters are pure functions in `@hewnui/themes/authoring`:

- `exportDesignMd`
- `exportDtcg`
- `exportTailwindTheme`
- `exportSkillMd`
- `THEME_EXPORT_FORMATS` — catalog with `tier: "free"` today

---

## Visual matrix

Source: https://hewnui.dev/docs/themes/matrix

Curated theme, mode, and material combinations for visual checks.

Only these combinations are supported. Use Theme Lab to inspect one row at a
time—never side-by-side theme matrices in the product UI.

## Supported rows

| Theme | Mode | Solid | Glass |
|-------|------|-------|-------|
| Forest | light | yes | yes |
| Forest | dark | yes | yes |
| Tide | light | yes | yes |
| Tide | dark | yes | yes |
| Graphite | light | yes | yes |
| Graphite | dark | yes | yes |
| Dune | light | yes | yes |
| Clay | light | yes | yes |
| Ember | dark | yes | yes |

## Motion overlay

Every row above can run with motion `on` or `off`. `prefers-reduced-motion`
forces the off path.

## Checklist

When reviewing visuals, confirm:

1. Accent remains singular and unsaturated
2. Glass keeps an opaque fallback
3. Dark packs use softer inner refraction edges
4. Numbers in tables stay tabular
5. Hit targets remain at least 40×40px

---
